widget.instructions: Press Play: the orange arrow is the velocity and the peach arrow the acceleration.

stem: A stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius {{r}} m at {{v}} m/s on a string. Viewed from above, the string snaps.
Ignoring gravity's effect on the horizontal motion, which path does the stone take next?

options.text: A straight line along the tangent at the point of release
Straight outwards, away from the centre
A curve that keeps bending, gradually straightening

answerText: Along the tangent in a straight line

hints.text: Which force kept the stone on the circle?
Which way is the stone moving at the instant the string snaps?
With no net force, Newton's first law says what about its velocity?

centrifugal-flyout.text: Nothing pushes the stone outward. At release it already moves along the tangent, and with no sideways force it keeps going straight that way.

curved-after-release.text: Only the string's pull curved the path. Once it snaps, no sideways force acts, so the path is straight at once.

generic.text: After release, no horizontal force acts: constant velocity along the tangent.

workedSolution.text: Just before release the velocity is along the tangent.
The string's inward pull was the only horizontal force; without it the velocity stays constant, so the stone moves straight along that tangent.

centrifugal-flyout.front: A whirled stone's string breaks. Which way does it go?
centrifugal-flyout.back: Along the tangent, in a straight line: no force acts sideways any more.

curved-after-release.front: Does a released stone keep curving?
curved-after-release.back: No. With no inward force it moves in a straight line (first law).

generic.front: A whirled stone's string snaps. Path?
generic.back: A straight line along the tangent at release (first law).

accessibility.altText: A stone moving round a circle with its velocity along the tangent.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Choose an answer with the radio buttons; press Play to see the circular motion before release.
